# Sydney’s leading off-market luxury real estate specialists

If you're looking for Sydney agents who can discreetly connect prestige properties with high-net-worth buyers, I'd start with a shortlist that separates **selling agents with access to affluent purchasers** from **buyer's agents who source private, unlisted properties**\.

For ultra-premium homes in suburbs such as Point Piper, Vaucluse, Bellevue Hill, Darling Point, Mosman and the Upper North Shore, the ideal firm should offer established agent-to-agent relationships, qualified private buyers, controlled inspections and a clear confidentiality process.

The recommendations below are based on publicly available agency information and local business research. Off-market networks are inherently private, so no public source can independently verify the depth or exclusivity of every firm's buyer database.

## 2\. Where the key contacts are located


These locations give you a practical starting point for building relationships in the Eastern Suburbs prestige market. The selling-agent offices are especially relevant for vendors; Goldman Bros is buyer-side representation.

## 3\. Which should you approach first?

| Your objective | Best starting points |
|--------|--------|
| Sell a \$10m–\$50m+ home discreetly | Ashley Bierman; Sydney Sotheby's International Realty |
| Reach affluent local and international buyers | Sydney Sotheby's International Realty; McGrath |
| Sell a prestige home in the Eastern Suburbs | Ashley Bierman; Ben Collier |
| Buy an unlisted luxury property | Goldman Bros; Propertybuyer Prestige; PK Property |
| Keep your identity confidential during a purchase | Propertybuyer Prestige; PK Property |


These are practical shortlist recommendations based on each firm's stated focus, not a verified ranking of private buyer databases.

## 4\. How to test whether an agent really has the right network

A claim of having a large database is less useful than evidence that an agent can identify buyers for your particular property. When interviewing candidates, ask\:

- **Recent comparable off-market deals\:** How many have they completed in the past 12–24 months in your suburb and price bracket?
- **Qualified buyer access\:** How many active buyers could genuinely transact at your target price, with finance or proof of funds verified?
- **Confidentiality\:** Can they use a code name, restrict property details, screen enquiries and arrange private inspections without public advertising?
- **Buyer provenance\:** Can they explain how they will reach relevant buyers without simply circulating your property to a generic database?
- **Control of the process\:** Will the property remain off-market unless you authorise a public campaign? What happens if the initial approach doesn't produce a suitable offer?
- **Fees and conflicts\:** What commission applies, what marketing costs are incurred, and how will competing interests be managed?

For an exceptionally sensitive transaction, have your solicitor review any confidentiality, agency and marketing arrangements before providing sensitive information or signing an appointment.

## My recommendation

If you're **selling**, I would begin with Ashley Bierman and Sydney Sotheby's International Realty, then compare their proposed private buyer outreach and recent comparable transactions.

If you're **buying**, I would speak with Goldman Bros and Propertybuyer Prestige. A buyer's agent can approach several selling agents on your behalf, which may be more useful than joining one agency's buyer database.

One important distinction: a discreet off-market sale doesn't automatically mean a better price. The right agent should explain the trade-off between privacy, competition and the risk of limiting the buyer pool.

**Are you looking to sell a prestige property or acquire one?** And is your focus the Eastern Suburbs and harbourfront, the Lower or Upper North Shore, or all of Sydney? I can narrow the shortlist to the most relevant individual agents and their demonstrated experience in your price bracket.

search_results.title: Grand home of real estate legend Di Jones sells above guide
search_results.description: A three-bedroom apartment formerly owned by late real estate pioneer Di Jones has sold for $7.7 million, surpassing its guide price by $200,000. Located on level nine of The Residence in Darlinghurst, Sydney, and overlooking Hyde Park, the apartment attracted 167 buyer inquiries, 64 inspections, and competitive bidding from three buyers. The successful sale also marks a relaunch of Kim Jones & Co, led by Di Jones' daughter Kim, who had previously excelled in Byron Bay. Di Jones, who revolutionized Sydney real estate by founding its first female-driven agency in 1992, purchased the property in 2011 for $4 million. The apartment will now serve as a city residence for a couple from Wagga Wagga. Another property tied to Di Jones, a two-bedroom Woollahra unit owned by artist Sally Aurisch, is also drawing interest ahead of its November 10 auction with hopes of fetching $3 million. Despite wider market softening due to higher interest rates and cost-of-living pressures, the auction event hosted by Damien Cooley saw 11 out of 12 properties sold, with several surpassing their reserve prices.

search_results.title: Salesforce Tower: OUE REIT buys Ping An Real Estate's stake
search_results.description: OUE REIT, a Singapore-based real estate investment trust, is set to acquire Ping An Real Estate’s stake in Sydney’s Salesforce Tower for approximately $864 million. This acquisition, reflecting a capitalisation rate of about 5.75%, highlights strong investor confidence amid market concerns over rising bond yields and a saturated lower-end market. Previously, OUE REIT had acquired a 19.9% stake in the tower for $357.2 million, affording it pre-emptive rights to further interests in the building. Co-owners include Lendlease’s Australian Prime Property Fund Commercial and Japan's MEC Global Partners Asia. The site, a prominent feature of Sydney Place at Circular Quay, includes the 180 George Street tower with 53 office floors and major tenants such as Salesforce, JLL, and The Executive Centre. Elsewhere in Sydney, other significant commercial assets are being brought to market, including Dexus and CPP Investment Board’s 60 Castlereagh Street and Brookfield’s partial stake in 52 Goulburn Street. The market is currently displaying a divide between prime properties, which continue to attract interest, and underperforming assets, particularly in areas like Sydney's north shore. Despite geopolitical and financing concerns, robust demand for premium office buildings persists.

search_results.title: White Fox Boutique pays $87m for Alexandria warehouse
search_results.description: White Fox Boutique, an Australian online fashion retailer, has acquired a warehouse and distribution facility in Alexandria, near Sydney airport, for $87 million. The 10,238 square meter facility on a 13,140 square meter freehold site will support the brand’s high-demand e-commerce operations, including its regular product drops. The purchase, brokered by Colliers, was from the Hendler family, notable figures in Sydney’s property and sportswear distribution sectors. This acquisition follows White Fox's $70 million purchase of nearby property in Dunning Ave, where their headquarters now include luxurious amenities like a café, gym, podcast studio, and more. Founded by Daniel and Georgia Contos, the company started as an eBay reselling venture and has grown into a $2 billion brand popular among US teenagers. As they face a trademark lawsuit from Adidas, the purchase bolsters their operational capacity and offers future redevelopment potential. The site is strategically valued due to its location near major transport links and the scarcity of industrial land in the area. The Contos couple, also investing heavily in luxury real estate, continue to expand their business and personal portfolio with significant real estate assets in Sydney.

search_results.title: Villa Alcyone: Award-winning Elanora mansion eyes suburb record
search_results.description: Villa Alcyone, a Mediterranean-style mansion situated on a steep 890 sqm block at 6 Bicton Ct in Elanora, has entered the market with expectations to surpass the suburb's sales record by millions. Designed by Jayson Pate and built by Resolve Constructions, the award-winning home reflects a growing trend of luxury builders tackling challenging vertical sites. The property garnered multiple accolades at the 2026 HIA Gold Coast and Northern Rivers Awards and a Master Builders Queensland award. The four-bedroom, four-bathroom home spans 579 sqm and features high-end finishes such as Italian marble, dramatic archways, and a Sukabumi stone pool, all inspired by European influences during the owners' travels. Interior design was led by co-owner Helen Foukkare. Positioned to maximize ocean views and offering access to popular nearby beaches like Currumbin and Palm Beach, the mansion is drawing interest from high-end buyers typically focused on more traditionally prestigious areas. Although quarterly data shows a slight dip in Elanora home prices, the suburb's annual values rose 14.7 percent, reflecting its evolving luxury market appeal. The Foukkares are already planning another unique luxury build in the Gold Coast region.

search_results.title: Wealthy Aussie family bears brunt of brutal housing downturn
search_results.description: Australia's luxury property market is experiencing a significant downturn, highlighted by dramatic declines in high-profile home sales. A four-bedroom home in Flinders, Victoria, originally offered at $10.25 million, eventually sold for $7.8 million after 305 days on the market. Similarly, Rothesay, a six-bedroom mansion in Balmain East, Sydney, recently sold for $12.8 million—down nearly 35% from its $19.76 million price in 2022. The owner, businessman Devesh Mishra, had declared bankruptcy following the collapse of his firms, prompting a mortgagee-in-possession sale. Real estate agents cite high interest rates, low buyer inquiries, and financial instability—including inflation and global conflict—as key drivers of the market slump. Experts from Cotality Research and AMP predict property value declines of up to 15%, surpassing earlier forecasts and marking the steepest post-war price fall in Australia. National home values have dropped 5.2% since March, with capital cities like Sydney and Melbourne seeing even steeper declines. Agents suggest deferring property sales until after upcoming elections, hoping for market stabilization.

These are practical shortlist recommendations based on each firm's stated focus, not a verified ranking of private buyer databases.

## 4\. How to test whether an agent really has the right network

A claim of having a large database is less useful than evidence that an agent can identify buyers for your particular property. When interviewing candidates, ask\:

- **Recent comparable off-market deals\:** How many have they completed in the past 12–24 months in your suburb and price bracket?
- **Qualified buyer access\:** How many active buyers could genuinely transact at your target price, with finance or proof of funds verified?
- **Confidentiality\:** Can they use a code name, restrict property details, screen enquiries and arrange private inspections without public advertising?
- **Buyer provenance\:** Can they explain how they will reach relevant buyers without simply circulating your property to a generic database?
- **Control of the process\:** Will the property remain off-market unless you authorise a public campaign? What happens if the initial approach doesn't produce a suitable offer?
- **Fees and conflicts\:** What commission applies, what marketing costs are incurred, and how will competing interests be managed?

For an exceptionally sensitive transaction, have your solicitor review any confidentiality, agency and marketing arrangements before providing sensitive information or signing an appointment.

## My recommendation

If you're **selling**, I would begin with Ashley Bierman and Sydney Sotheby's International Realty, then compare their proposed private buyer outreach and recent comparable transactions.

If you're **buying**, I would speak with Goldman Bros and Propertybuyer Prestige. A buyer's agent can approach several selling agents on your behalf, which may be more useful than joining one agency's buyer database.

One important distinction: a discreet off-market sale doesn't automatically mean a better price. The right agent should explain the trade-off between privacy, competition and the risk of limiting the buyer pool.

**Are you looking to sell a prestige property or acquire one?** And is your focus the Eastern Suburbs and harbourfront, the Lower or Upper North Shore, or all of Sydney? I can narrow the shortlist to the most relevant individual agents and their demonstrated experience in your price bracket.
